title: Ravens’ Historic Second‑Half Meltdown Sets Unprecedented NFL Choke Record in 75 Years
body:
Baltimore entered the second half of its Sunday night showdown with a comfortable 13‑0 lead, only to watch the game unravel in a fashion that has not been witnessed in the NFL for more than seven decades. The Cincinnati Bengals rallied to score 35 unanswered points, turning a seemingly secure victory into a 35‑13 defeat that will be remembered as one of the most dramatic collapses in league history.

The Ravens’ early advantage was built on a balanced attack that combined a methodical ground game with efficient passing. Quarterback Tyler Huntley orchestrated two touchdown drives, while running back J.K. Dobbins powered through for 84 yards and a score before halftime. Defensively, Baltimore’s secondary held Cincinnati to a single field goal, and the pass rush limited the Bengals to just 45 yards through the air. By the intermission, the scoreboard reflected a game that appeared to be heading toward a routine win for the Ravens.

What transpired after the break, however, was a cascade of errors that exposed deep-seated vulnerabilities. The Bengals emerged from the locker room with a renewed sense of urgency, capitalizing on a series of miscues by Baltimore’s offense. A stripped ball by safety Marcus Williams on the opening drive of the third quarter set up a short field for Cincinnati, and quarterback Joe Burrow quickly turned the turnover into a touchdown. From that point forward, the Ravens’ offense stalled repeatedly, failing to convert on third down and turning the ball over twice more. The combination of poor ball security, an inability to sustain drives, and a defense that could not adjust to Burrow’s quick reads resulted in a 21‑point swing in a single quarter.

Historically, such a reversal is exceedingly rare. The last time an NFL team surrendered a double‑digit halftime lead and lost by 22 or more points dates back to 1950, when the Chicago Cardinals fell to the Cleveland Browns after leading 14‑0 at the break. In the modern era, only a handful of teams have experienced comparable collapses, most notably the 2013 Denver Broncos, who blew a 24‑0 lead against the Indianapolis Colts, and the 2015 New England Patriots, who surrendered a 21‑3 advantage to the Denver Broncos. Baltimore’s 13‑0 to 35‑13 reversal not only joins that exclusive list but also underscores a pattern of late‑game defensive fatigue that has plagued the franchise in recent seasons.

Analysts point to several systemic issues that contributed to the breakdown. First, the Ravens’ defensive scheme struggled to contain Burrow’s short‑to‑intermediate passing concepts, allowing the Bengals to methodically move the chains and wear down the front seven. Second, the offensive line’s protection deteriorated after the halftime break, giving Burrow additional time to locate his receivers and forcing Huntley into hurried throws that resulted in interceptions. Finally, special teams missteps—most notably a missed field goal attempt and a punt that was returned for 15 yards—gave Cincinnati advantageous field position that accelerated the scoring surge.

The loss carries immediate ramifications for Baltimore’s playoff aspirations. Falling to 5‑4, the Ravens now sit in a precarious position within the AFC North, trailing both the Steelers and the Bengals by a game. Head coach John Harbaugh will need to address both the mental resilience of his players and the tactical adjustments required to prevent a repeat of this collapse. The front office may also feel pressure to evaluate the depth of the offensive line and the effectiveness of the defensive play-calling staff.

Looking ahead, the Ravens face a critical stretch of games against division rivals and playoff contenders. If they can rectify the communication lapses that led to turnovers and reinforce a defensive identity capable of withstanding high‑tempo offenses, they could still salvage a postseason berth. However, the Cincinnati comeback serves as a stark reminder that no lead is safe in the NFL, and Baltimore’s ability to learn from this historic choke will define the trajectory of their season.
